nodes.title: Orthonormalizable Banach modules
nodes.statement: Construct c_A(I), the A-valued families tending to zero outside finite sets with the supremum norm, and its universal property: continuous A-linear maps c_A(I) → M correspond to bounded families of vectors of M.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
A ≠ 0; the zero ring is handled by the convention on p. 8 (the zero module counts as ONable of arbitrary rank).
proofSteps: Sum a coefficient family against a bounded vector family using nonarchimedean convergence.
Recover a continuous map from its values on the coordinate vectors; the operator norm is the supremum of their norms.
Describe continuous maps between such modules by bounded matrices whose output coefficients tend to zero for every input coordinate.
acceptance: Prove existence, uniqueness, completeness and the operator-norm formula.
Treat an arbitrary index set; do not silently restrict to countable bases.

nodes.title: Finite submodules and coordinate approximation
nodes.statement: A finitely generated submodule P of an orthonormalizable Banach A-module is closed. For every ε>0 there is a finite coordinate projection π_T with ‖π_T(p)−p‖ ≤ ε‖p‖ for all p in P.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
The ambient Banach module is orthonormalizable.
proofSteps: Use Noetherianity on the coordinate columns of finitely many generators to find a finite projection injective on P.

Compare P's subspace norm with its finite-module Banach topology through that projection: with Q the finite module P in its canonical Banach topology, Q → P → A^S is continuous by Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.1(b) (BGR 3.7.3/2–3), and the image in A^S is closed by BGR Proposition 3.7.3/1, so the two norms on P are equivalent and P is closed in M.
Apply the nonarchimedean open mapping theorem to a finite free presentation and rescale by a fixed element of K of norm less than one.
acceptance: Prove the uniform estimate for every p, not just for the chosen generators.
Verify the finite-module topology and open-mapping inputs before using closedness.

sources.excerpt: P is a closed subset of M

nodes.title: Completely continuous matrix criterion
nodes.statement: For a continuous map between orthonormalizable A-Banach modules, compactness in the sense of operator-norm limits of finite-rank maps is equivalent to sup_i |a_ij| tending to zero as the output index j leaves finite sets.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
Use the source’s matrix convention φ(e_i)=Σ_j a_ij f_j.
proofSteps: The coefficient condition gives finite-rank approximations π_Tφ in operator norm.
For the converse first reduce to finite-rank maps, then apply uniform coordinate approximation on a finite submodule containing the image.
Pass to the operator-norm closure.
acceptance: Keep complete continuity distinct from unproved equivalence with a topological compact-image definition.
Do not drop Noetherianity: the source explicitly leaves that extension open.

nodes.title: Fredholm determinant from finite minors
nodes.statement: For a compact endomorphism φ of an orthonormalizable A-Banach module, construct P_φ(T)=det(1−Tφ) as the convergent sums of principal minors and prove that it is entire with constant coefficient one.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
φ is an operator-norm limit of finite-rank endomorphisms.
proofSteps: Form each coefficient as the signed sum of determinants indexed by finite subsets of the basis.

Use decay of the matrix columns to prove coefficient summability and convergence for every scalar radius: let r_1 ≥ r_2 ≥ … be the decreasing rearrangement of r_j = sup_i |a_ij| (which tends to zero by the matrix criterion); each product over an n-element index set involves n distinct column indices, so |c_n| ≤ r_1⋯r_n and |c_n|R^n ≤ (r_1R)⋯(r_nR) → 0 for every R > 0 (Serre, Proposition 7 b). The estimate uses only |ab| ≤ |a||b| in A and transfers verbatim; Serre's own definition of the series (reduction of a norm-≤1 operator modulo ideals of the valuation ring and a projective limit of finite-rank determinants) is replaced in the source by the direct minor formula.
Compare finite-coordinate truncations with ordinary finite-dimensional determinants.
acceptance: The rank-finite specialization recovers the algebraic determinant.
Prove |c_n|r^n→0 for every r>0, rather than only convergence on one disc.

nodes.title: Determinants independent of bases and norms
nodes.statement: The Fredholm determinant of a compact endomorphism depends only on the Banach-module topology. It is unchanged by choosing a different orthonormal basis or an equivalent norm that makes the module orthonormalizable.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
proofSteps: Prove continuity of the determinant under operator-norm limits.
Compare a finite-rank endomorphism with its algebraic determinant on a finite free submodule containing its image.
Approximate simultaneously in the two equivalent norms to pass from algebraic invariance to the infinite-dimensional determinant.

nodes.title: Cyclic determinant identity
nodes.statement: If u:M→N is compact and v:N→M is continuous between potentially orthonormalizable Banach A-modules, both composites are compact and det(1−Tuv)=det(1−Tvu).
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.

Lemma 2.7 is printed for ONable modules; the potentially ONable case follows by choosing equivalent ONable norms, since compactness and the determinant depend only on the topology (Corollary 2.6 and p. 17). The (Pr) case is Lemma 2.12, left as an exercise in the source.
proofSteps: Reduce the compact map to finite rank by determinant continuity.
Approximate its image inside finite coordinate submodules.
Approximate v only on the relevant finite submodule, then apply the finite-dimensional cyclic determinant identity.

nodes.title: Completed base change of Banach modules
nodes.statement: A continuous map A→B of commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebras sends a potentially orthonormalizable module M to M ⊗̂_A B with transported basis. Compact maps stay compact and their Fredholm determinants are obtained by applying A→B coefficientwise.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
B is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.

The completed tensor product M ⊗̂_A B and its norm are used without definition (BGR §2.1.7); the proof of Lemma 2.8 needs only that |Σ_{i∈S} e_i ⊗ b_i| is bounded by a constant multiple of max_i |b_i|.
proofSteps: Construct mutually inverse maps between c_A(I) ⊗̂_A B and c_B(I) using finite sums and completion.
Transport the matrix of a compact map and apply the column-decay criterion.
Pass the coefficient map through the convergent determinant sums.
acceptance: Prove the comparison for continuous coefficient maps; contractivity is not required in the potentially orthonormalizable formulation.
Keep this determinant base-change theorem separate from the later Hecke-image base-change theorem.

nodes.title: Banach direct summands

hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
proofSteps: Use the open mapping theorem to lift bounded vector families through a surjection.
Apply the lifting characterization to a finite free presentation for the converse implication.

Also prove the claim stated without proof on p. 18 that a finite projective A-module with its Banach topology has (Pr).

nodes.title: Fredholm theory on Banach direct summands
nodes.statement: Extend the Fredholm determinant to compact endomorphisms of (Pr) modules by adding a zero operator on a complement. Prove independence of the complement, multiplicativity on direct sums, the cyclic identity and completed base change.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
All Banach modules carrying determinants satisfy (Pr).
proofSteps: Compare two complements inside their common larger orthonormalizable direct sum.
Use conjugation and the determinant of a zero summand to establish independence.
Reduce the cyclic and scalar-extension identities to the potentially orthonormalizable results.
acceptance: The determinant on a finite projective module agrees with its algebraic determinant.

Supply actual proofs for the exercises in Lemmas 2.12–2.13 and for the two ingredients stated without proof on pp. 19–20: the determinant of φ ⊕ 0 on M ⊕ N equals that of φ (immediate from the matrix definition with the union basis), and det(1 − X(φ ⊕ ψ)) = det(1 − Xφ)det(1 − Xψ) for compact φ, ψ on (Pr) modules (Serre, Lemme 2 of §5, in the field case).

nodes.title: Entire functions and analytic resultants
nodes.statement: Construct the entire series ring A{{T}}, division by a monic polynomial and the resultant Res(Q,P) for monic Q and entire P. Prove that Res(Q,P) is a unit exactly when Q and P generate the unit ideal.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
proofSteps: Normalize coefficients, prove polynomial division first, and pass to convergent truncations.
Define the resultant through elementary symmetric functions, equivalently the norm of P in A[T]/(Q).

Use the resultant's Bézout identity and multiplicativity to prove the unit criterion: Res(Q,P) ∈ (Q,P) is proved for polynomial P from Lang, Algebra, Ch. IV §8 and extended to entire P by writing P = BQ + R with R a polynomial (Lemma A3.5); conversely if fQ + gP = 1 then 1 = Res(Q, gP) = Res(Q,g)·Res(Q,P) (Lemma A3.7).
acceptance: Keep uniform convergence estimates under coefficient scaling.
Do not assume A{{T}} is complete for the unit-disc supremum norm.

nodes.title: Fredholm resolvents and spectral invertibility
nodes.statement: For a compact φ on a (Pr) A-Banach module and a monic Q, Q is coprime to P_φ in A{{T}} exactly when Q*(φ) is invertible, where Q*(X)=X^deg(Q)Q(X^−1).
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
M satisfies (Pr).

The forward direction uses P_v = D(1−Q*, P_φ) for v = 1 − Q*(φ) (Coleman Theorem A3.9, stated for orthonormizable modules and proved by reduction modulo I ∈ I(A), which for a K-Banach algebra contains ρA^0) and D(1−Q*, P_φ)(1) = Res(Q, P_φ) (Lemma A3.8 (11), Q monic); for a (Pr) module apply them to φ ⊕ 0, using that the polynomial 1−Q* has zero constant term.

The converse direction (Q*(φ) invertible ⇒ (Q, P_φ) = 1) writes Q*(φ)(1−w) = 1, notes w = v(w−1) is compact, and needs det(1−v)·det(1−w) = det((1−v)(1−w)) = 1 for the commuting compact v, w (Serre §5, Corollaire 1 to Proposition 7; Coleman Corollary A2.1.1, cited as A2.2.1 in the proof of Lemma A4.1). Buzzard's §2 neither states nor proves this product identity in the Noetherian Banach/(Pr) setting; see the gap 'Product multiplicativity of Fredholm determinants'.
proofSteps: Construct the entire operator-valued resolvent F(X) = P_φ(X)/(1−Xφ) = Σ v_m X^m with v_0 = 1 and v_m = c_m + φ v_{m−1}, so each v_m ∈ A[φ]; Serre's Lemme 3 gives |v_m| ≤ r_1⋯r_m by the adjugate (Cramer) formula in finite rank, then for finitely supported columns, then by a limit, hence |v_m|R^m → 0 for all R (Proposition 10). The argument uses only matrix entries in A and the identity |φ| = sup|a_ij| (p. 9), so it transfers to ONable A-modules, and to (Pr) modules via φ ⊕ 0, whose resolvent is F(X) ⊕ P_φ(X)·1.
Apply polynomial spectral mapping to v=1−Q*(φ); evaluate its resolvent identity at one.
Combine the resulting resultant identity with the unit criterion; reverse the argument using an inverse for Q*(φ).
acceptance: Prove convergence in operator norm before evaluating the resolvent.
The reciprocal polynomial convention must match the later eigenvalue coordinate.

nodes.title: Riesz projectors at a Fredholm root
nodes.statement: If a is a root of order h of P_φ in the Hasse-derivative sense, split M=N⊕F into closed φ-stable summands with (1−aφ)^h=0 on N and 1−aφ invertible on F. Construct the projectors in the operator-norm closure of A[φ], and prove N is finite projective of rank h. For h > 0, a is a unit and det(1−Tφ|N) = (1−a^{−1}T)^h.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
M satisfies (Pr).
The h-th Hasse derivative at a is a unit and all lower derivatives vanish.
a ∈ A (Serre: a ∈ K, where 'unit' reads 'non-zero'); for h ≥ 1 the definition forces a ∈ A^× (p. 22).
proofSteps: Following Serre's Proposition 12, which Buzzard says goes through unchanged: apply the divided derivatives Δ^s to (1−Tφ)F(T) = P_φ(T) and evaluate at T = a, obtaining v_s := Δ^sF(a) with (1−aφ)v_0 = 0, (1−aφ)v_s − φv_{s−1} = 0 for 0 < s < h and (1−aφ)v_h − φv_{h−1} = c := Δ^hP_φ(a), a unit; hence (1−aφ)^{s+1}v_s = 0 for s < h. Put e = c^{−1}(1−aφ)v_h and f = −c^{−1}φv_{h−1}: then e + f = 1 and f·e^h = 0, so p = e^h and q = (e+f)^h − e^h are complementary projectors in the closure of A[φ], with (1−aφ)^h q = 0 and (1−aφ)^h v_h^h = c^h p; set N = ker p = im q and F = im p. All operators involved commute.

Serre then bounds dim N(a) ≤ h using that every finite-dimensional φ-stable subspace of c(I) is complemented with quotient again of the form c(J) (Remarque 2 of §1, a field-specific fact) together with Lemme 2 of §5; Buzzard diverges here: (1−aφ)^h = 0 on N expresses the identity of N as a polynomial in φ without constant term, hence compact on the (Pr) module N; a finite-rank α with |1 − α| small is invertible (Neumann series in the complete algebra Hom(N,N), 'elementary argument' on p. 23), so N = α(N) is finitely generated.

Use (Pr) to obtain projectivity (Lemma 2.11), then factor P = P_N·P_F (multiplicativity on direct sums) and apply Lemma 3.1 to φ|_F with Q = (T−a)^h to see (1−a^{−1}T)^h coprime to P_F, hence dividing P_N, and by uniqueness of division dividing it in A[T]; write P_N = D·(1−a^{−1}T)^h and P = (1−a^{−1}T)^h·G, so D | G in A{{T}} and D(a) is a unit; φ is invertible on N so det(φ|N) ∈ A^× and the leading coefficient of D is a unit; reducing modulo each maximal ideal, (1−āφ̄)^h = 0 forces P̄_N = (1−ā^{−1}T)^{rank}, so D̄ = 1, the rank is h, and D = 1 (constant term 1).
acceptance: Generalized eigenspaces and the exact power h remain visible.
Handle h=0 separately; for h>0 prove that a is a unit.

nodes.title: Finite projective slope summands
nodes.statement: If P_φ(T)=Q(T)S(T), where Q(0)=S(0)=1, Q is a degree-n polynomial with unit leading coefficient and (Q,S)=1, construct the unique closed φ-stable splitting M=N⊕F with Q*(φ)=0 on N and invertible on F. Prove N finite projective of rank n and det(1−Tφ|N)=Q(T).
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
A is a commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebra.
M satisfies (Pr).
S is entire and Q is relatively prime to S in A{{T}}.
proofSteps: Set v = 1 − Q*(φ)/Q*(0) = B(φ) with B ∈ T·A{{T}} (Q*(0) is the unit leading coefficient of Q); spectral mapping (Coleman Theorem A3.9, applied to φ ⊕ 0 for a (Pr) module) gives P_v = D(B,Q)·D(B,S) = (1−T)^n·D(B,S), and D(B,S)(1) = Res(Q/Q*(0), S) by Lemma A3.8 (11) for the monic polynomial Q/Q*(0), a unit by Lemma A3.7 since (Q,S) = 1; hence 1 is a zero of order n of P_v in the divided-derivative sense.
Apply the Riesz root splitting to v to obtain rank n and initially a power-annihilation statement.

Factor determinants: P_F is coprime to Q by Lemma 3.1 applied to φ|_F (with the monic Q/Q*(0)), so Q divides P_N = G in A{{T}}; G is a polynomial of degree ≤ n (N projective of rank n) with G(0) = 1, and uniqueness of division by the monic Q/Q*(0) gives G = Q; Cayley–Hamilton on the rank-n projective N then gives Q*(φ) = 0 on N, improving the power-annihilation Q*(φ)^n = 0 delivered by Proposition 3.2.
acceptance: Prove the exact annihilator Q*, not merely a power of Q*.
Show every operator commuting with φ preserves both summands because the projectors lie in the closure of A[φ].

gaps.title: Determinant estimates and Riesz projector construction in Serre (now read)
gaps.detail: R1b-review read Serre, Publ. Math. IHÉS 12 (1962), Propositions 7–8 (§5), 10 (§6) and 11–12 (§7) with their proofs, in the Numdam copy (SHA-256 67a032…). Setting: K complete non-archimedean with non-trivial valuation, E a Banach space isomorphic to c(I), u completely continuous; discreteness of the valuation is assumed only in Propositions 1, 2, 5, 9, 13, 15, none of which Buzzard uses. What transfers verbatim to Noetherian K-Banach algebras: the coefficient formula and the estimate |c_m| ≤ r_1⋯r_m (Proposition 7 a, b), the finite-rank comparison (7 d), the uniform coefficient estimate |c_m^{(n)} − c_m| ≤ ε (Proposition 8), the recurrence v_m = c_m + u v_{m−1} and the bound |v_m| ≤ r_1⋯r_m for the resolvent (Proposition 10, Lemme 3), the resolvent identity H(a) = (1−au)P(a,u) (Proposition 11) and the divided-derivative construction of the projectors p = e^h, q = (e+f)^h − e^h (Proposition 12). What does not transfer and is replaced in Buzzard: Serre's definition of det(1−tu) by reduction modulo ideals of the valuation ring (Buzzard uses the minor formula directly), and the count dim N(a) = h, which uses Remarque 2 of §1 (finite-dimensional subspaces of c(I) are complemented with quotient c(J)) and Lemme 2 of §5; Buzzard replaces it by compactness of the identity on N, Lemma 2.11 and the reduction-modulo-maximal-ideals argument on pp. 23–24. Still unread: Serre §§2–4 (the field-case matrix criterion, Propositions 3–6), Proposition 9 and §§8–9.

gaps.title: Product multiplicativity of Fredholm determinants
gaps.detail: The converse direction of Lemma 3.1 (Coleman Lemma A4.1, which Buzzard says 'goes through unchanged') writes Q*(φ)(1−w) = 1 and uses det(1−v)·det(1−w) = det((1−v)(1−w)) = 1 for the commuting compact operators v = 1 − Q*(φ) and w. Serre proves this (Corollaire 1 to Proposition 7) by reduction modulo ideals of the valuation ring in the field case; Coleman states it as Corollary A2.1.1 (cited as A2.2.1 in the proof of A4.1) for orthonormizable modules by the same reduction. Buzzard's §2 contains no statement of it. R1b-review sketched a proof in Buzzard's toolkit: approximate v and w by π_T v and π_T' w (Lemma 2.3(c)), whose images and the image of π_T v + π_T' w − π_T v π_T' w lie in the finite free coordinate module A^{T∪T'}; Lemma 2.5(b) identifies all three Fredholm series with algebraic determinants on that module, where the product rule holds; Lemma 2.5(a) (uniform coefficient convergence, i.e. Serre's Proposition 8) then passes the identity, evaluated at X = 1, to the limit; the (Pr) case follows via φ ⊕ 0. This route has not been written out and the packet does not claim it; until it is, Lemma 3.1's converse rests on an unstated import.

gaps.title: Nonarchimedean open mapping and finite-module topologies
gaps.detail: Buzzard Proposition 2.1 invokes Bourbaki, EVT I §3.3 Théorème 1 (open mapping, with 'homomorphisme' meaning strict morphism) and Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert Propositions 3.7.3/2–3; Lemma 2.3(b) also uses BGR 3.7.3/1 (submodules of finite Banach modules are closed), p. 6 uses BGR 3.7.2/2 (ideals of A are closed), p. 8 uses BGR Corollary 2.1.8/3 (bounded = continuous) and Lemma 2.8 uses the completed tensor product of BGR §2.1.7. The precise Noetherian Banach hypotheses are retained, but this pass has not decomposed those cited proofs. Existing coefficient norm constructions must be checked for the required module generality.

gaps.title: Polynomial spectral mapping in the corrected generality
gaps.detail: Coleman's §A3 (division, resultants, Lemmas A3.5, A3.7, A3.8 and Theorem A3.9) was read by R1b-review. Theorem A3.9 (P_{B(u)} = D(B, P_u) for B ∈ T·A{{T}}) is stated for orthonormizable E over a Banach algebra with I(A) ≠ ∅ and proved by reduction modulo I ∈ I(A) followed by a limit; for a K-Banach algebra ρA^0 ∈ I(A) since ρ ∈ K^× is multiplicative. Buzzard asserts (p. 20) that §A3 applies to commutative Noetherian K-Banach algebras and uses A3.9 through Lemma 3.1 and in Theorem 3.3 (where the monic polynomial is Q/Q*(0), so that D(B,S)(1) = Res(Q/Q*(0), S) by A3.8 (11)); for (Pr) modules the identity must be transported through φ ⊕ 0, which is legitimate because B(0) = 0. The reduction-modulo-ideal proof of A3.9 presupposes that Coleman's construction of P_u agrees with Buzzard's minor formula (it does, by Serre Proposition 7 a). The transport of every convergence and spectral-mapping step must still be written out before claiming proof-plan closure; nothing contradictory was found.

libraryReview.scope: Local Mathlib Analysis and Geometry text searches plus the existing Fredholm-operator files were inspected. No declaration was type-checked as supplying this nonarchimedean affinoid Fredholm-determinant machine. All node implementation statuses stay unchecked.

review.notes: All 13 nodes and 17 original links checked against Buzzard §§2–3 (SHA-256 re-verified), Coleman §A3–A4 and Serre 1962 §§1, 5–7 (Numdam PDF fetched and hashed, Propositions 7–8 and 10–12 read with proofs); 9 nodes verified, 4 corrected in place (cyclic-determinant-identity, projective-banach-modules, fredholm-resolvent, riesz-root-projectors); no node was removed or added. Two links added for direct uses at the cited locations (fredholm-resolvent → finite-slope-summands, Lemma 3.1 on p. 25; summand-fredholm-theory → riesz-root-projectors, P = P_N P_F on p. 23); link graph checked acyclic and all endpoints exist; the three PadicFamilies.json links consuming this packet's nodes point at existing node IDs. Most important finding: Lemma 3.1's converse imports the product multiplicativity of Fredholm determinants (Serre Cor. 1 to Prop. 7 / Coleman Cor. A2.1.1) which Buzzard's §2 never states; recorded as a new gap with a sketched but unwritten proof route, not disguised as an input. Serre's Prop. 12 dimension count is field-specific (Remarque 2 of §1) and Buzzard's replacement argument was checked. No contradiction remains; packet status stays partial because the locally analytic distribution modules and compact semigroup operators (the rest of L4) are unread, the BGR/Bourbaki inputs are undecomposed and the exercises 2.12–2.13 are unproved. Details in research/expansion/reviews/eigenvariety-review.md.
